subject: Creativity
title: The Double Diamond: Diverge, Converge, Repeat
description: Learn The Double Diamond: Diverge, Converge, Repeat in one minute.

hook.text: The British Design Council mapped how designers work: two diamonds — first find the right problem, then the right solution.

buildup.text: Diamond 1: Discover widely (diverge), then Define precisely (converge).

discovery.text: Most teams jump straight to solutions. The Double Diamond forces them to spend equal time understanding the problem.

twist.text: The model looks linear but isn't. Teams loop back constantly — discovering mid-delivery that they defined the problem.

climax.text: It's used by governments (UK, Singapore), corporations (IBM, Google), and NGOs worldwide — a universal creative.

punchline.text: Two diamonds: one for the problem, one for the solution.

quiz.question: What does the first diamond in the Double Diamond model focus on?
options: Finding and defining the right problem

details.summary: The double diamond model structures innovation into four phases across two diamonds: discover and define the right problem, then develop and deliver the right solution. Each diamond diverges to explore broadly, then converges to focus narrowly.
details.whyItMatters: The double diamond provides a clear visual framework for navigating the messy creative process. It shows that innovation requires spending as much effort defining the problem as solving it.
takeaways: First diamond: discover broadly then define the real problem
Second diamond: develop many solutions then deliver the best one
Divergent and convergent phases alternate throughout the process

faq.question: Who created the double diamond model?
faq.answer: The British Design Council published the double diamond framework in 2005 after studying the design processes of eleven major companies. It has since become one of the most widely used design process models worldwide.

faq.question: How is the double diamond different from design thinking?
faq.answer: They overlap significantly. The double diamond is a visual framework for the process structure. Design thinking, as taught by Stanford's d.school, adds specific methods like empathy research and rapid prototyping. Both emphasize iteration and user-centricity.
